project.name: YariZan — یاریزان
project.tagline: Persian educational mini-game launcher with hardware-bound activation and encrypted game assets.
project.summary: A .NET 9 WPF launcher for grades 1–6, designed as an RTL leather-book experience with HWID-bound ECDSA activation, AES-256-GCM encrypted game packages, trial mode, packaging tools and installer workflow.

caseStudy.problem: Educational mini-games needed a polished Persian launcher that organizes content by grade while preventing casual sharing of purchased content and activation files.
caseStudy.solution: Create a WPF book-style launcher backed by machine-bound signed activation, encrypted game blobs, a packer tool, a serial-generation tool and a controlled decrypt-run-cleanup execution flow.
highlights: Six grade catalog with extensible game discovery

challenges.title: Offline machine activation
challenges.description: Serials must validate locally without shipping the private signing key.
challenges.resolution: Sign a versioned HWID payload with ECDSA-P256 and ship only the public key in the launcher.

challenges.title: Protecting packaged games
challenges.description: Bundled game executables should not be trivially extractable from the installation directory.
challenges.resolution: Encrypt games with AES-256-GCM, decrypt on demand to a restricted temporary directory and clean up after execution.

challenges.title: Persian visual metaphor
challenges.description: The application should feel like a physical educational book while preserving correct RTL reading order.
challenges.resolution: Build a custom WPF book interface with RTL layout, Shabnam font and page-oriented navigation.

results: Self-contained launcher, activation and packaging toolchain
Explicit threat model documents realistic DRM limits
Repository includes architecture, security, build and CI documentation

architecture.summary: The solution separates the WPF launcher from a core security/domain library and two operator tools: SerialGen signs machine activation and Packer transforms source mini-games into encrypted distributable assets.

recruiter.headline: Desktop product engineering combining UX, cryptography, tooling and deployment workflow.
talkingPoints: Separates runtime, core security logic and operator tools
Uses public-key signatures so the private signing key never ships
Documents threat-model limits instead of overstating DRM security
